question: colorless Plastids are called?
solution:
The correct answer is **__leucoplastids__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **L**eucoplastids

 
 
• ​Leucoplasts are organelles found in plant cells and belong to the plastid family. In contrast to other plastids like chloroplast, they lack** pigmentation**.
 
• They are referred to as amyloplasts, elaioplasts, or proteinoplasts (also known as aleuroplasts), depending on whether they are specialized for the **bulk storage** of protein, lipid, or starch.
 
• Leucoplasts serve a wide range of essential **biosynthetic function**s and do not serve a major storage function in many cell types.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plastids**

 
 
• ​The plastid is a membrane-bound organelle that is found in the cells of some** eukaryotic organisms,** including plants, algae, and bacteria.
 
• **Cyanobacteria** that live inside cells are known as intracellular endosymbiotics.
 
• Leucoplasts are non-pigmented plastids that can occasionally differentiate,** chromoplasts** are used for pigment synthesis and storage, and chloroplasts are used for photosynthesis.
